notes.claim: The synchronous speed of the turning field is 120 f / p rpm for f hertz and p poles; an induction motor's shaft runs a little slower than it.
In a series motor the same current flows through field and armature, and its speed can climb to dangerous levels if it runs without a load.
A motor that is turning also acts as a generator; the emf it makes is called back emf and it opposes the supply.

sources.title: Electrical Induction Motors - Synchronous Speed
sources.quote: The speed of an induction motor is therefore limited to a speed below synchronous speed and the difference between synchronous speed and actual speed is called slip .

sources.title: Electric motor - Synchronous, Rotating Fields, AC Motors | Britannica
sources.quote: The effect of the stator current is to establish a magnetic field rotating at 120 f / p revolutions per minute for a frequency of f hertz and for p poles.

sources.title: Your motor sheet: the DC series motor
sources.quote: A DC series motor is a type of direct current electric motor where the armature and field windings are connected in series, so the same current flows through both.

sources.title: 23.6 Back Emf - College Physics for AP® Courses 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: It is zero when the motor is first turned on, meaning that the coil receives the full driving voltage and the motor draws maximum current when it is on but not turning.

sources.title: 23.6 Back Emf - College Physics for AP® Courses 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: The motor thus acts as a generator whenever its coil rotates.

sources.title: Your motor sheet: the DC series motor
sources.quote: A key characteristic is its poor speed regulation; the motor's speed varies significantly with load and can increase to dangerous levels if the motor runs without a load.
